content.title: Dick Vitale Sends Message After Cameron Boozer News
content.text: Duke Blue Devils star Cameron Boozer had a spectacular season in the collegiate ranks, averaging 22.4 points on 56.3% shooting, 10.3 rebounds and 4.2 assists per game.Boozer ranked third in the nation in scoring with 806 points and fourth in rebounding with 371. He also had 21 double-doubles.AdvertisementBoozer was named the ACC Player of the Year and ACC Rookie of the Year. He also earned the ACC Tournament's MVP award after leading the Blue Devils to the conference title against Virginia, 74-70.On Tuesday, Boozer added to his college basketball accolades. He received the Oscar Robertson Trophy as the USBWA National Player of the Year. According to Duke, he was the fifth player in program history to win the honor as a freshman, joining Cooper Flagg, Zion Williamson, Anthony Davis and Kevin Durant.Duke Blue Devils forward Cameron Boozer (12) exits the court after defeating the Pittsburgh Panthers.Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images (Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images)Duke has 10 winners of the Oscar Robertson Trophy, the most by any team. The U.S. Basketball Writers Association started giving out the recognition in 1959.AdvertisementRenowned broadcaster and former basketball coach Dick Vitale reacted to the honor.Vitale, who served as coach of the University of Detroit and the Detroit Pistons, expressed his belief that Boozer was the right choice for the award. He was also full of praise for the youngster, whom he called a flat-out winner."Yes absolutely the right choice," Vitale commented on Duke's post. "Cameron has been special ALL year. A flat out winner!Vitale is undoubtedly one of the most recognizable figures in college basketball, and his opinion carries a lot of weight. His recognition of Boozer speaks volumes about what the Duke star has done in his freshman year.AdvertisementRelated: Duke Makes First-Ever Announcement Before NCAA TournamentThis story was originally published by Athlon Sports on Mar 25, 2026, where it first appeared in the College Basketball section.
